stories.title: Treasury's latest bid to calm the bond market fails to convince investors
stories.summary: The Treasury made another attempt to calm a rattled bond market, but investors are not buying it, according to MarketWatch. CNBC reports the 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since 2004 as the bond market rout continues.
stories.whyItMatters: A deepening bond rout raises borrowing costs across the economy and signals investors doubt the government's ability to steady the market.
whatToWatch: Whether the 30-year yield keeps climbing past its 2004 high
Any further Treasury action to steady the market
questions: What specifically has the Treasury proposed to calm markets?
